name: LiteLLM
cost: Open source. A paid Enterprise license adds SSO, support and other features.
works_with: Python, any OpenAI-compatible client, and 100+ LLM providers
short: Call 100+ LLM providers through one OpenAI-style API, as a Python library or as a self-hosted gateway with cost tracking.
what: LiteLLM gives you one interface for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure and many more, all in the OpenAI format. You can use it as a Python SDK, or run the proxy server as a gateway for a team with virtual keys, spend tracking, guardrails, load balancing and an admin dashboard. It can also route MCP tools and A2A agents.
who: Developers who call more than one model provider, and teams who want one place to manage keys and spending. If you only ever use one provider through its own SDK, you probably don't need it.
needs: An API key for each provider you want to call

steps.title: Call a model
steps.text: Set your provider keys as environment variables, then call `completion` with a `provider/model` name.
steps.code:
from litellm import completion
import os

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "your-openai-key"
os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] = "your-anthropic-key"

# OpenAI
response = completion(model="openai/gpt-4o", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}])

steps.title: Or run the gateway
steps.text: This starts the proxy server. Point any OpenAI client at `http://0.0.0.0:4000`.

try.label: From the README
try.text: With the gateway running, create `openai.OpenAI(api_key="anything", base_url="http://0.0.0.0:4000")` and send a chat completion to `gpt-4o` with the message "Hello!".

watch: You store your provider API keys with LiteLLM, either as environment variables or in the gateway.
Some gateway features fall under the LiteLLM Commercial License, not the open source one.
If you deploy the Docker image, the README shows how to verify its signature with cosign first.
